name: HM Land Registry Use land and property data
fact: HMLR portal exposes bulk registered-land datasets including INSPIRE polygons, local land charges, National Polygon Service, ownership, leases, covenants and price-paid data.
gate: Dataset availability does not itself create a canonical parcel relation; individual licence, freshness and geometry caveats still apply.

name: HMLR INSPIRE Index Polygons dataset
fact: INSPIRE polygons show the indicative position and extent of registered freehold property and provide an INSPIRE ID linkable to title information.
gate: HMLR states the polygons are indicative, not exact legal title boundaries; title register/plan verification remains required.

name: HMLR July 2026 INSPIRE polygon download
fact: The current download page states the INSPIRE files were published 5 July 2026 and new files are published on the first Sunday of each month.
gate: Monthly freshness does not convert indicative index polygons into exact legal boundaries.

name: HMLR public data catalogue
fact: HMLR lists Price Paid Data, Transaction Data, UK HPI, INSPIRE polygons and other datasets under public or licensed access and explicitly warns that fitness for a particular purpose is not guaranteed.
gate: Source-quality caveats must be retained for parcel scoring.

name: HMLR Price Paid Data current release
fact: Price Paid Data was updated 26 June 2026 with May 2026 transactions; HMLR warns the current month should not be used in isolation because later registrations update the picture.
gate: Sale-price records are transaction evidence, not development permission or current site availability.

name: HMLR Price Paid Data collection
fact: The official collection links current Price Paid Data and explains that it contains sale prices submitted to HMLR for registration.
gate: Only sales lodged for registration and sold for value are represented.

name: HMLR Registered Leases
fact: Registered Leases records leasehold land/property, lease date and term; leases over seven years generally require registration, and the dataset is updated monthly.
gate: Lease registration is a tenure/control signal, not proof of development availability or possession rights for a project.

name: HMLR Registered Leases technical specification
fact: The technical specification states the dataset covers registered leasehold land/property and uses a UID that can link to other HMLR datasets; address relationships may produce multiple rows.
gate: UID linkage still requires exact title and geometry reconciliation.

name: HMLR Restrictive Covenants
fact: The dataset identifies registered titles with restrictive covenants but does not disclose the covenant terms; it is updated monthly.
gate: Presence alone cannot determine development impact; the underlying register/document must be inspected.

name: HMLR Restrictive Covenants technical specification
fact: The technical specification says the dataset covers registered land/property with a covenant and its UID is consistent across HMLR datasets for relational linking.
gate: The dataset excludes the actual covenant wording, so legal effect is not inferable from the flag alone.

name: HMLR UK companies owning property
fact: The dataset covers registered land/property owned by UK companies or corporate bodies and is updated monthly after registration changes are completed.
gate: Corporate ownership is not evidence of willingness to sell, development control or current project status.

name: HMLR UK-company ownership technical specification
fact: The schema exposes title number, tenure, address, proprietor fields and change dates, while HMLR documents possible company-number and proprietorship data errors.
gate: Company identifiers require cross-checking; no parcel promotion from ownership data alone.

name: HMLR overseas companies owning property
fact: The dataset covers completed records where non-UK companies/corporate bodies own registered land/property and is updated on the second working day of each month.
gate: It excludes private individuals, UK companies with overseas addresses and charities; ownership does not equal development availability.

name: HMLR overseas-company ownership technical specification
fact: The technical specification defines inclusion of registered legal estates held by companies/corporate bodies incorporated outside the UK.
gate: Exact title linkage and current register status are required before use.

name: HMLR National Polygon Service
fact: The National Polygon Service includes National Polygon, Title Descriptor and Title Number-UPRN lookup datasets and reports more than 25 million titles and 28 million polygons.
gate: The service is licensed and its polygons are indicative representations, not exact legal title boundaries.

name: HMLR National Polygon technical specification
fact: HMLR states every registered title has at least one index polygon and that polygon extents may be the same size, larger or smaller than the title-plan extent.
gate: Index polygons must never be treated as exact boundaries without title-plan/legal verification.

name: HMLR Local land charges spatial data INSPIRE
fact: The dataset maps indicative locations of migrated local land charges including environmental restrictions, legal land-use agreements, TPOs and protected-site charges.
gate: Coverage is incomplete while authorities migrate; definitive charge extent requires source documents from the originating authority.

name: HMLR July 2026 Local land charges download
fact: The current LLC INSPIRE download was published 6 July 2026 and is refreshed on the sixth of each month as more authorities migrate.
gate: Absence from the download may reflect migration coverage rather than absence of a charge.

name: HMLR land-property data API information
fact: The HMLR REST API can list datasets, metadata and secure download links for company ownership, National Polygon Service, restrictive covenants and registered leases after licence/access setup.
gate: API availability does not bypass dataset licences or exact-title validation.

name: HMLR land registration data collection
fact: The collection groups HMLR ownership, sales/transaction and spatial datasets, including Price Paid, UK HPI, INSPIRE and National Polygon Service.
gate: Collection-level discovery is not parcel evidence by itself.

name: Planning Data public transport access node dataset
fact: Planning Data reports 363,324 NaPTAN public-transport access nodes and a collector run on 23 July 2026, while the dataset page labels the platform origin as MHCLG-created pending authoritative replacement.
gate: Use exact DfT-authoritative entity records and route/service evidence rather than dataset presence alone.

name: DfT transport node entity 50060929
fact: DfT-authoritative node 50060929 is named Railway Station, entry date 25 June 2026, with a precise point and NaPTAN code.
gate: A node point does not establish service frequency, capacity, walk-time or parcel accessibility score.

name: DfT transport node entity 50268585
fact: DfT-authoritative Railway Station node 50268585 has entry date 3 June 2026 and precise point/NaPTAN metadata.
gate: Requires route/service and exact parcel accessibility analysis.

name: DfT transport node entity 50133797
fact: DfT-authoritative Railway Station node 50133797 has entry date 15 July 2026 and precise coordinates.
gate: Node presence alone is not a Future Growth uplift.

name: DfT rail access node entity 50132013
fact: DfT-authoritative Rail Station node 50132013 has entry date 1 July 2026, a precise point and transport-access-node type RSE.
gate: Parcel-level travel-time and service evidence remain required.

name: DfT transport node entity 50172538
fact: DfT-authoritative Rail Station node 50172538 has entry date 9 June 2026 and precise NaPTAN point metadata.
gate: Node presence alone is not connectivity evidence sufficient for promotion.

name: DfT transport node entity 50268931
fact: DfT-authoritative Rail Station node 50268931 has entry date 2 June 2026 and precise point metadata.
gate: Exact parcel routing/service analysis remains required.

name: DfT transport node entity 50031452
fact: DfT-authoritative Railway Station node 50031452 has entry date 8 July 2026 and precise point/NaPTAN metadata.
gate: A station point is not a measured accessibility score.

name: DfT transport node entity 50034665
fact: DfT-authoritative Railway Station node 50034665 has entry date 2 June 2026 and precise point/NaPTAN metadata.
gate: Exact parcel relation and service quality remain required.

name: DfT transport node entity 50265150
fact: DfT-authoritative Railway Station node 50265150 has entry date 9 July 2026 and precise point metadata.
gate: No promotion from node proximity without routing/service analysis.

name: DfT transport node entity 50127997
fact: DfT-authoritative Station node 50127997 has entry date 1 July 2026 and precise NaPTAN point metadata.
gate: Node presence alone does not quantify accessibility uplift.

name: Planning Data local plan dataset
fact: Planning Data reports 1,047 current, emerging or historical local plans from 63 providers, with new data found 22 July 2026, but labels the platform origin MHCLG-created pending authoritative replacement.
gate: Use the authority's current adopted/emerging plan and dates for parcel policy assignment.

name: Barking and Dagenham Site Allocation Proformas
fact: Planning Data indexes Barking and Dagenham Local Plan 2037 Appendix 2 Site Allocation Proformas with entry date 9 February 2026 and authority document links; quality is 'some'.
gate: Read the authority document directly before assigning a site allocation or capacity.

name: Planning Data site category taxonomy
fact: The site-category dataset currently contains two categories, deliverable and hazardous-substances, and notes some MHCLG-created data.
gate: Taxonomy is classification context only and cannot establish a hazardous-substance constraint at a parcel.

name: Planning Data mineral safeguarding area dataset
fact: The Planning Data mineral-safeguarding-area page currently reports zero records, zero providers and no collection attempt.
gate: No-data must not be interpreted as no mineral safeguarding constraint; use mineral planning authority policies/maps.

name: Planning guidance: land affected by contamination
fact: Official planning guidance requires contamination implications to be considered so sites are suitable for use and unacceptable pollution risks are addressed; site-specific investigation may be required.
gate: Only a competent site investigation/risk assessment can establish contamination at a specific parcel.

name: Environment Agency voluntary remediation advice
fact: Published 3 June 2026, the EA service offers site-specific regulatory advice where land contamination has impacted controlled waters outside certain planning/discharge consultations.
gate: Availability of advice is not evidence that a parcel is contaminated or remediated.

name: Planning guidance: land stability
fact: Guidance identifies landslide, subsidence and ground-heave risks and notes that plans/applications may require land- or slope-stability risk assessment and mitigation.
gate: Exact ground conditions require site investigation and relevant mining/geotechnical evidence.

name: Planning guidance: noise
fact: Noise is relevant where development creates noise or is sensitive to the prevailing acoustic environment; good acoustic design should be considered early.
gate: Noise impact is proposal- and location-specific; generic numerical criteria are not universal fixed thresholds.

name: Travel Plans, Transport Assessments and Statements guidance
fact: Guidance states developments generating significant movement should be supported by proportionate Travel Plans and/or Transport Assessments/Statements, with residual severe impacts potentially relevant to refusal.
gate: Requirement and severity are case-specific and need local network evidence.

name: Planning guidance: minerals safeguarding
fact: Mineral planning authorities should identify Mineral Safeguarding Areas and policies to prevent unnecessary sterilisation, potentially including prior extraction where appropriate.
gate: Exact safeguarding status must come from the relevant mineral authority policies map, not the empty Planning Data layer.

name: DfT Local transport plans statutory guidance
fact: Published 2 April 2026, the statutory guidance explains legal duties, evidence-based plan preparation, implementation and links between transport, funding and local objectives.
gate: LTP policy is area-level evidence and must be translated to exact schemes/sites before scoring.

name: DfT Local transport plans detailed guidance
fact: The 2026 guidance directs authorities to align transport with local plans/SDS, use the Connectivity Tool, identify well-connected locations and target interventions supporting future growth/regeneration.
gate: Connectivity and planned interventions still require exact site/scenario evaluation.

name: Road Investment Strategy 3: 2026-2031
fact: RIS3 covers April 2026 to March 2031 and commits £27 billion for the strategic road network, including resilience, congestion and growth/housing objectives.
gate: National programme funding is not proof that a specific parcel receives a road intervention.

name: National Highways performance report 2025-26
fact: Published 16 July 2026, the report covers National Highways performance from 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026, including capital enhancements, renewals and operations.
gate: Network performance context is not a parcel-level transport unlock.

name: DfT Connectivity Tool
fact: Updated 3 July 2026, the tool combines transport and land-use data to score connectivity for locations in England and Wales and can test new transport routes.
gate: A connectivity score must be run for the exact location/scenario; generic nearby-node evidence is insufficient.

name: DfT Connectivity Tool application guidance
fact: DfT states the tool was designed for spatial/transport planning, tested with more than 40 local authorities and can help locate development and assess transport interventions.
gate: Tool methodology/results must be applied to exact canonical sites before promotion.

name: Ofgem demand connections reform update
fact: Published 16 June 2026, Ofgem says the demand queue is large/growing, includes non-viable projects and can delay well-progressed demand connections; reform aims to curate and prioritise viable/strategic demand.
gate: System reform is macro connection context; exact DNO/NESO connection evidence is required for a parcel/project.

name: Ofgem demand connections call-for-input outcome
fact: Ofgem's June 2026 update summarises 120 responses and says emerging views are not final policy decisions.
gate: Do not treat consultation options as implemented connection rules.

name: Ofgem Gate 2 Whole Queue timetable decision
fact: Decision published 3 June 2026 allows phased Gate 2 connection offers through 2026 with the final batch expected by mid-March 2027 and requires progress/risk reporting.
gate: Timetable does not establish an individual project's queue position or connection date.

name: Ofgem connections reform and battery capacity update
fact: Published 17 April 2026, the joint DESNZ/Ofgem letter records connections-reform progress and battery-storage oversupply in the reformed queue.
gate: Queue-wide evidence is not individual site connection proof.

name: Ofgem ED3 business-plan guidance
fact: Published 21 May 2026, Ofgem sets business-plan requirements for DNOs for ED3 (2028-2033), with draft/final determinations expected in 2027.
gate: Planned network investment is not an existing connection offer or current local headroom measurement.
